title: bug: a claimed task whose pre-flight get_context payload exceeds 128 KiB can never launch, because the wrapper passes it as one CLI argv string (E2BIG, exit 126)
description:
Observed 2026-10-31 02:02-02:12Z. Filed by governor-4764040b. It blocks [CQ-R13] f4811a72, the CQ-R epic's integration row.

Symptom:
- worker-25da16b2 and then worker-c75a6f39 each claimed f4811a72.
- Each failed 3 times in a row, with "worker session ended ... (CLI exit=126) ... MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LAUNCH_FAILURE_BOARD_ONLY" within seconds of launch.
- Each then went into launch outage and released the row. The next idle coder would have been the third victim.
- Other rows launched fine on the same seats and bytes. c7ee939a's payload is 69,719 bytes.

Mechanism, measured:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh builds DYNAMIC_CONTEXT, which embeds the full pre-flight get_context JSON in a <claimed_task_context> block (around :7830). It is prepended to the user prompt, which reaches the CLI as ONE argv string. The claude cmdline in /proc shows the whole block.
- Linux caps a single argv string at 131,072 bytes (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). Above that, execve fails with E2BIG and bash exits 126. Repro: `/bin/true "$(head -c 140000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a)"` gives rc 126 and "Argument list too long"; 130,000 bytes gives rc 0.
- f4811a72's get_context payload is 140,812 bytes. task.epicSiblings is 82,904 of it (34 CQ-R siblings, about 2.4K each). epicRails is 10,466 bytes and appears twice, in epic.epicRails and allRails.epic.
- Any epic that grows past about 35 siblings, or any task with a large plan or comments, hits the same wall. Every seat that claims such a row is knocked into launch outage in turn.
- The ps1 twin has to be checked as well: Windows caps the whole command line at 32,767 chars.

The fix is the planner's call. Examples:
- (a) Both wrappers stop inlining a payload past a safe bound: write it to a temp file the agent reads, or tell the agent to call moe.get_context itself.
- (b) Daemon side, bound the default packet. epicSiblings is the bulk; packetManifest already measures a 100000-char budget but never acts on it.
(a) is the minimum, because it removes the failure class.
definitionOfDone: Regression in both launcher harnesses (postflight.sh and postflight.ps1): a claimed task whose fake get_context payload exceeds 131072 bytes launches the CLI without exit 126, and the session still gets its context, either inlined under the bound or through a file or fetch instruction. RED on the parent.
A payload under the bound is passed exactly as today, byte for byte, so prompt-cache behaviour for normal tasks is unchanged.
After landing, CQ-R13 f4811a72 launches on a worker seat. The completion summary names the payload size that was measured.
